---
title: "Summary · Nervous System"
---

## Key takeaways

- The **Nervous System** completes the Part 3 Pico progression:
  Identity → Senses → Mind → Voice → Hands → Nervous System. It is
  the event-driven fabric across which a Pico senses, communicates, and
  coordinates with many other participants.
- **Hands** change external systems (one capability, one target, one
  action). The **Nervous System** senses, communicates, and coordinates
  (many participants, many messages, many-to-many). They are not
  synonyms.
- The **Pico Agent Transport** is provider-neutral. The Pico depends on
  a stable semantic vocabulary — **observation**, **event**, **command**,
  **delegation**, **result**, **presence**, and **discovery** — not on
  MQTT topic strings, broker client IDs, or vendor-specific message
  formats.
- **Discovery** is a first-class Pico capability: a Pico can advertise
  its capabilities and be found by others without hard-coding a peer
  list.
- **Identity before delivery**: no message is trusted without identity
  and authorization context. A Pico identity is independent of MQTT
  client IDs, broker sessions, and all infrastructure identifiers.
- **Authorization boundary**: broker authentication ("can this client
  publish here?") is not Open Engineering authorization ("is this Pico
  permitted to observe, command, or delegate this?"). The two remain
  separate keys, decisions, and audit trails.
- **Memory is not a side-effect of delivery**: the Pico classifies each
  message (discard, observe, store, delegate, act). Delivery is a
  communication concern; classification and retention are cognitive
  concerns.
- **EMQX/MQTT is a candidate adapter**, not the semantic owner. Every
  runnable check in this wave operates on local YAML; no broker is
  provisioned; no credentials are used.

## The governing principle

```
Open Engineering owns the semantics.
Infrastructure providers implement the transport.

A Pico advertises its capabilities.
A Pico advertises its presence.
Another Pico discovers it.
Messages carry provider-neutral meaning.
Identity binds every message.
Authorization gates every command and delegation.
Delivery is not memory.
The transport is an adapter, not a runtime dependency.
```
